title: Boolean counter loop run to completion
statement: Let $M$ be a deterministic machine with $k$ Boolean work tapes and state $a$, and let $exit$ be an optional state. Let $w$ be a Boolean word with binary value $d$, and suppose the extra tape initially agrees with the word buffer at cells $cp+p$ for every integer $p$ with $-1\\le p\\le |w|$. Given an initial configuration $c$ and a run-length function $\\tau$, suppose each round $r<d$ starts in state $a$, has positive length, and at every positive time strictly before its endpoint has a state different from $a$ and not equal to the designated exit; also suppose each next round configuration is in state $a$. If $T$ equals the sum of these round lengths plus $\\operatorname{overhead}(w,d+1)$, the Boolean counter-loop machine reaches its done configuration at time $T$, with the extra tape set to true on cells $cp$ through $cp+|w|-1$. Before time $T$ its state is neither done nor escape; through $T$ the extra head remains in $[cp-1,cp+|w|]$, and the first $k$ work-head positions at each time match a run of $M$ from some round configuration, with either $r<d$ and $u\\le\\tau(c_r)$ or $r=d$ and $u=0$.

The specified total time $T$ equals the round-length sum plus counter overhead
